name: Vaishali Restaurant
why_it_matters: 31-year-old pure-veg multi-cuisine restaurant near the Maha Bodhi School — Sarnath's most-cited independent sit-down. Practical answer for the international Buddhist pilgrim flow that needs a sit-down meal between visits to the Dhamek Stupa and the Mulagandhakuti Vihara.
insider_tip: Opens 7am — the only spot offering breakfast in the Sarnath core. Stick to north Indian; the south Indian is competent but the kitchen runs it less often.
signature_address: Sarnath Road, near Mahabodhi School, Sarnath 221007

name: Aditya Restaurant
why_it_matters: Long-running pure-veg restaurant at Sarnath Chauraha — the road junction most pilgrim taxis pass through coming from Varanasi. Useful for a quick lunch close to the Buddhist sites without trekking back to Varanasi.
insider_tip: Best for a fast turnaround — counter-service speed. Skip during the main day-tour rush (12-2pm); Sarnath day-trippers from Varanasi all stop here at the same time.

name: Mahabodhi Society Dharmashala canteen
why_it_matters: The Sri Lanka Mahabodhi Society's dharmashala (pilgrim guesthouse) maintains a basic canteen on Sarnath's main road, opposite the deer park. Modest, low-cost vegetarian meals primarily for resident pilgrims but open to visitors when meals are being served.
insider_tip: Set meal times only — typically lunch 12-1:30pm and dinner 7-8:30pm. Treat it as a pilgrim canteen rather than a restaurant; portion sizes and menu vary day to day.
signature_address: Sarnath main road, opposite Deer Park, Sarnath 221007

name: Hotel Mrignayanee restaurant
why_it_matters: UP Tourism's Hotel Mrignayanee runs an in-house restaurant — the standard government-tourism choice in Sarnath, used by foreign-pilgrim packages routed through state tourism. Reliable AC dining when independent options run out.
insider_tip: Easier to book a table here mid-afternoon between the lunch and dinner rushes. UP Tourism also runs the larger Hotel Rahi Tourist Bungalow nearby with similar dining.
